scenes.heading: Evidence for evolution
scenes.sub: Rocks, bones, embryos and DNA all tell the same story
scenes.say: How do scientists know species change over time and are related? Rocks, bones, embryos, DNA and where animals live all point to the same answer: living things share common ancestors.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: In a pile of clothes, the bottom shirt was dropped first
scenes.science: In undisturbed rock layers, lower fossils are older
scenes.breaks: rock layers take thousands to millions of years, and they can be folded or flipped, so the rule only works when undisturbed.
scenes.say: Think of a pile of clothes on your floor. The shirt at the bottom went in first. Sedimentary rock builds up the same way, so lower fossils are older. That's relative dating. Radioactive isotopes give the actual age in years. That's absolute dating.

scenes.heading: Fossils
points: Form when buried quickly in mud or sand
Many past species are now extinct
The record has gaps: fossils are rare
scenes.say: Fossils usually form when an organism is buried quickly. They show many species are now extinct. Transitional fossils like Archaeopteryx, with feathers but also teeth and a bony tail, show features of two groups. Gaps are expected, because fossilisation is rare.

scenes.heading: Homologous vs analogous

left.title: Homologous
points: Human arm, bat wing, whale flipper

scenes.say: Homologous structures share the same bone plan but do different jobs, like the five-digit limb of a human, bat and whale. That shows a common ancestor. Analogous structures do the same job but are built differently, like bird and insect wings. That's convergent evolution.

scenes.heading: Leftovers and embryos
points: All have a tail and pharyngeal arches
scenes.say: Vestigial structures are leftovers, like your tailbone or the tiny pelvic bones inside whales. And early embryos of fish, birds and humans look surprisingly alike, all with a tail and folds in the neck called pharyngeal arches.

scenes.heading: DNA comparison
scenes.question: A 100-base gene section is compared. Differences from species W: X = 3, Y = 12, Z = 27. Which is most closely related to W?
lines: Mutations build up after species split
X is closest; Z is most distant
scenes.say: Mutations build up after two lineages split. So fewer DNA differences mean a more recent common ancestor. If species X differs from W by three bases and Z by twenty-seven, X is the closest relative. Fewer differences, closer cousins.
scenes.caption: Mutations build up after two lineages split. So fewer DNA differences mean a more recent common ancestor. If species X differs from W by 3 bases and Z by 27, X is the closest relative. Fewer differences, closer cousins.

scenes.heading: Biogeography
points: Southern continents were joined in Gondwana
Look-alikes can fool you: the thylacine
scenes.say: Biogeography is where species live and why. Australia was once part of Gondwana. After it separated, its marsupials evolved in isolation. The thylacine looked like a wolf but was a marsupial: convergent evolution, not close relationship.

points: Fossils, Body parts, Embryos, DNA, Distribution
scenes.say: Quick recap. Five lines of evidence: fossils, body parts, embryos, DNA and distribution. They all point to common ancestors. Now try the practice questions!
